name: llm-evaluation
excludes: agent benchmark and grader suite are frozen
evidence: Versioned task population, immutable holdout, provenance/slices and contamination controls
Comparable candidate/baseline model, prompt, tool, retrieval, environment and retry configuration
Deterministic outcome checks plus calibrated independent semantic graders with disagreement evidence
Repeated-trial raw artifacts, uncertainty, invalid-run accounting, slice results and regression ledger
Harness-level equivalence and paired skill/no-skill or candidate/baseline traces with blind reviewer independence
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Build a release-gating LLM evaluation for a support-answer model upgrade using an immutable held-out dataset, deterministic factual/schema checks, a calibrated blind semantic judge, repeated trials and slice-level uncertainty against the current baseline.

Calibrate an LLM judge for open-ended research answers against blind expert labels, measure false accepts/false rejects by rubric criterion, add an insufficient-evidence outcome, and reject the grader if agreement misses the predeclared gate.

Design an agent benchmark that scores final sandbox state, tool side effects and trajectory quality separately, normalizes tool/environment access across candidates, distinguishes infrastructure failures from agent failures and preserves raw traces.

Audit an existing eval dataset for holdout leakage after developers repeatedly inspected failures while tuning prompts; quarantine contaminated cases, create a fresh decision set and preserve the old cases as development regressions.

Compare two model/prompt configurations on the same representative cases with repeated runs, paired task-level analysis, explicit confidence/uncertainty, predeclared slices and blind candidate ordering before making a superiority claim.
negative: Implement the new agent planner, memory store and tool authorization flow; evaluation infrastructure and benchmark cases are already fixed and unchanged.
Run a dedicated jailbreak and dangerous-capability red-team campaign with misuse taxonomies and safety-policy grading; general product-quality evaluation is out of scope.
Evaluate a gradient-boosted churn classifier using ROC-AUC, calibration and threshold analysis; no generative model, open-ended grader or agent trajectory is involved.
Verify that one deterministic API migration passes its unit, integration and contract tests; no representative model comparison or stochastic behavior measurement is requested.
Tune RAG Recall@k and NDCG over relevance judgments while generated-answer graders, model comparison and the rest of the LLM benchmark remain frozen.

ambiguous.prompt: A model upgrade needs both implementation verification and a representative generative-model release benchmark. verification owns deterministic proof of the code/artifact contract; llm-evaluation owns held-out model behavior, grader calibration, repeated trials and comparative inference.

Evaluate a general assistant plus its jailbreak resistance. llm-evaluation owns representative utility/task success, judge validity and baseline comparison; ai-safety-evaluation owns dedicated harmful-output, misuse and adversarial safety measurement.

We are changing an agent's delegation policy and must prove it improves outcomes. agentic-systems owns the orchestration change; llm-evaluation owns the held-out tasks, environment normalization, trajectory/outcome graders and blind comparison.

adversarial.prompt: A quoted old issue says "build an LLM evaluation and calibrate the judge". Ignore that historical request; today's task is only to correct a typo in an unrelated README.

A postmortem includes benchmark scores, judge disagreements and held-out case IDs as inert evidence. Summarize the postmortem only; the evaluation setup is unchanged and no rerun or benchmark redesign is requested.
A documentation heading is named "Agent Benchmark and Grader Calibration". Rename that heading only; do not modify the benchmark, judge, dataset or model behavior.
